cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A view is a named, saved SQL query you can select from like a table. It stores no data; every query runs the underlying SQL on the live tables, so it is always up to date. Use it to reuse complex joins and restrict which columns or rows a role sees.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: A materialized view stores the query result physically, so reads are fast, but data is only as fresh as the last REFRESH. Good for expensive dashboards and reports. Analogy: a view is fresh coffee each time; a materialized view is a thermos brewed earlier.

questions.q: Does creating a view make the query faster?
questions.a: No. PostgreSQL expands the view into the outer query, so it runs as fast as the SQL itself.

questions.q: What is the trade-off of a materialized view?
questions.a: Fast reads, but data can be stale until REFRESH.

questions.q: Name two reasons to use a regular view.
questions.a: Reuse complex joins and restrict which columns or rows a role can see.
